title: Argid laa er laa
description: Ten short stories about everyday money: a fish stall in Peel that takes euros, a farm shop selling oatmeal and fleeces, an election diary about taxes and merit pay, the price of new glasses, a man who gambles his wages away, a mother's money-saving blog, a small travelling circus short of money, a museum that finds mammoth bones and a sponsor, a charity parachute jump for a hospice, and paid online lessons during a quarantine.

lessons.title: Boiddagh son y thie-oast
lessons.summary: Osian Keig sells fish from a stall on the edge of the quay in Peel until noon; he is quick with his knife, has a chat with Tirion Prowse, the landlady of an inn, who buys cod every Friday, takes euros from an Irish tourist, and catches her when she slips on the wet quay, while guillemots and a sandpiper watch from the rocks.
lessons.text:
Ta Osian Keig creck eeast ayns Pheeil. Ta'n boayrd echey ny hoie er ymmyl y keiy, faggys da ny baatyn. Dy chooilley voghrey, t'eh goaill yn eeast veih ny eeasteyryn, as t'eh creck eh derrey munlaa. Ec munlaa, t'eh glenney y boayrd as goll thie.

Jiu, ta ram boiddee echey. Haink ny boiddee veih baatey e vraar, as t'ad feer noa. Ta Osian bieau lesh y skynn. Ayns un minnid, t'eh giarey boiddagh mooar ayns ayrnyn.

Haink benainshtyr y thie-oast dys y boayrd: Tirion Prowse. She ish benainshtyr y thie-oast mooar er y traie. T'ee kionnaghey eeast veih Osian dy chooilley Jeheiney, son dy vel ny turrysee laccal eeast son nyn shibbyr. Ghow ad cowag veg mychione yn emshir, mychione y thie-oast as mychione ny baatyn. S'mie lesh Tirion cowag, as s'mie lesh Osian cowag neesht, agh ta'n traa giare roish munlaa.

“Ta feme aym er kiare boiddee jiu,” dooyrt Tirion. “Ta'n thie-oast lane.”

“Ta boiddee mie aym,” dooyrt Osian. Ghiare eh ad dy bieau, as hug eh ad ayns paagey. Ren Tirion eeck son yn eeast, as ghow ad cowag elley mychione e moir.

Eisht haink ben aeg veih Nerin, Ciara. She turrysagh v'ee. Cha row punt erbee eck, agh va oarey eck. “Vel shiu goaill oarey?” dooyrt ee.

“Ta,” dooyrt Osian. “Ta ram turrysee veih Nerin çheet dys Pheeil 'sy tourey, as ta oarey ec dagh fer jeu. Ta mee goaill oarey as punt.” Ren Ciara kionnaghey boiddagh beg er jeih oarey.

Va'n keiy fliugh lurg y fliaghey. Ren Ciara çhyndaa, as skyrr ee er ny claghyn fliugh. Va ee faggys da ymmyl y keiy, agh ghow Tirion greim er e laue. “Ta'n keiy fliugh,” dooyrt Tirion. “Ta sleih skyrrey ayns shoh dy mennick.”

Va Ciara gennal. Cha row ee er skyrrey dys yn ushtey.

Er ny creggyn faggys da'n keiy, va ram stronnagyn. Ta ny stronnagyn doo as bane, as t'ad soie er ny creggyn er yn ymmyl. Va looyran beg roie er y traie, bieau myr y gheay. Va'n looyran shirrey bee 'sy gheinnagh. Ren Ciara jeeaghyn er ny stronnagyn as er y looyran son tammylt.

Ec munlaa, va ooilley ny boiddee creckit. Ren Osian yn argid y choontey: punt as oarey. Ren eh glenney y boayrd, as hie eh thie.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n boayl ta boayrd Osian?
Ta'n boayrd echey er ymmyl y keiy ayns Pheeil.
Quoid boiddee ren Tirion kionnaghey?
Ren ee kionnaghey kiare boiddee son y thie-oast.
Cre'n argid va ec Ciara?
Va oarey eck, as cha row punt erbee eck.
Cre haink er Ciara er y keiy fliugh?
Skyrr ee er ny claghyn fliugh, agh ghow Tirion greim er e laue.
Cre va'n looyran jannoo?
Va'n looyran shirrey bee 'sy gheinnagh.

lessons.title: Yn shapp beg er y thalloo
lessons.summary: Ifan Trelease and his daughter Mali open a small shop on their farm near Ramsey because the big market pays too little: they sell oatmeal ground from their own oats, fleeces, piglets from the sow's new litter and seedlings of deciduous trees, keep the old plough by the door, and watch a kestrel over the ridges of the field while a cockerel with sharp spurs guards the yard.
lessons.text:
Ta Ifan Trelease cummal er thalloo beg faggys da Rhumsaa marish e inneen, Mali. Ta kirree, muc as kellee oc, as ta corkey oc 'sy vagher mooar. Rish ymmodee bleeantyn, va Ifan creck ooilley yn eeym echey ec y margey mooar. Agh cha row'n margey eeck dy liooar. Va'n leagh echey ro injil, as va costys y vee son ny baagh goll seose dy chooilley vlein.

“Lhisagh shin shapp beg y yannoo ayns shoh er y thalloo,” dooyrt Mali un fastyr. “Foddee sleih çheet dys y thalloo, as foddee shin creck roo gyn margey erbee.”

Ren ad shen. Ren ad shenn hie y ghlenney, as ren ad boayrd mooar y hoie 'sy çheu sthie. Faggys da'n dorrys, hug ad yn shenn traaue. Va'n traaue shen ec ayr Ifan, as ec e ayr roish. Cha nel ymmyd jeant jeh'n traaue nish, agh s'mie lesh ny paitçhyn jeeaghyn er.

Hoshiaght, ta meinn ayns y shapp. Ta'n chorkey çheet veih'n vagher oc, as ta mwyllin beg ec Ifan. T'eh jannoo meinn chorkey jeh, as ta Mali cur y veinn ayns paagyn. Ta meinn vie oc, as ta sleih kionnaghey ee son arran as son bee moghree.

Ta loamrey ayns y shapp neesht. Tra ta Ifan giarey ollan ny kirree 'sy tourey, ta dagh loamrey çheet jeh'n cheyrrey slane. Ta mraane ta jannoo snaie kionnaghey ny loamrey.

'Sy tourey shoh, va aalagh noa ec y vuc: nuy arkanyn beggey. Ta Ifan freayll kiare arkanyn, as t'eh creck yn chooid elley jeh'n aalagh da eirinee elley. Ta ny arkanyn roie mygeayrt y garey.

Ec y dorrys, ta sheelagyn ayns paagyn beggey. Ta Mali goaill rassyn veih ny biljyn 'sy ghlion, as t'ee cur ad 'sy thalloo derrey t'ad nyn sheelagyn. She biljyn tuittymagh ad: tra ta'n fouyr çheet, ta ny duillagyn tuittym jeu. Ta sleih kionnaghey ny sheelagyn shoh son nyn garaghyn, as ta Mali gra roo: “Ta biljyn tuittymagh lhome 'sy gheurey, agh bee ad glass reesht 'syn arragh.”

Ta'n magher oc jeant jeh immyr er immyr: ta dagh immyr ard as lhean, as ta coan beg eddyr daa immyr. Ta stannair çheet dy mennick, as t'eh croghey 'syn aer er-y-chione y vagher. Ta'n stannair shirrey lughee. Ta Ifan jeeaghyn er y stannair, as t'eh gra: “T'eh gobbraghey son y thalloo, as cha nel eh geddyn argid erbee.”

Ta kellagh mooar ec y thie neesht. Ta spuir geyre er dagh cass echey. Tra ta moddey noa çheet dys y garey, ta'n kellagh roie huggey, as ta'n moddey goll ersooyl. Ta'n spuir beg, agh t'eh geyre.

Lurg un vlein, ren Ifan yn argid y choontey. Va ny smoo argid oc na roie, as va ny kionneyderyn gennal.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ren Ifan as Mali shapp y yannoo?
Er-y-fa nagh row'n margey mooar eeck dy liooar.
Cre ta Ifan jannoo lesh y chorkey?
T'eh jannoo meinn chorkey jeh 'sy vwyllin echey.
Quoid arkanyn va 'syn aalagh noa?
Va nuy arkanyn beggey 'syn aalagh.
Cre ta taghyrt da biljyn tuittymagh 'sy fouyr?
Ta ny duillagyn tuittym jeu.
Cre ta'n stannair shirrey?
Ta'n stannair shirrey lughee er-y-chione y vagher.

lessons.title: Lioar-laa yn reihys
lessons.summary: In her diary, Morvoren Pascall describes standing for a seat in the House of Keys: she knocks on doors to talk to voters about the island's budget and taxes, polishes her speech when her friend Dewi says it is full of repetition, refuses the old enmity between the parties, argues that pay should follow merit and not the norm, and in the end the voters choose her for the post.
lessons.text:
Jelune, 3 Mee Houney. Ta mee er chur my ennym roish y theay. Ta mee laccal staartey ayns Kiare as Feed. Cha nel mee er ve my oltey roie, as ta aggle orrym, agh ta mee jeant magh. Ta ram reihderyn ayns my ard, as ta feme aym loayrt rish dy chooilley reihder.

Jeheiney, 7 Mee Houney. Hie mee mygeayrt ny thieyn rish shiaght oor jiu. Ta ny reihderyn loayrt mychione argid er y chooid smoo: keeshyn, costys y vee, as leagh ny thieyn. Dooyrt un reihder dy vel e vac aeg gobbraghey ayns Doolish, agh nagh vel argid dy liooar echey dy chionnaghey thie. Ta mee smooinaghtyn dy vel y feysht shoh feer symoil, as feer scanshoil neesht.

Jesarn, 8 Mee Houney. Ren mee my oraid y lhaih da Dewi, my charrey. Ren eh clashtyn rish dy kiart. “Ta aaloayrtys ayns dty oraid,” dooyrt eh. “T'ou gra ‘keeshyn injil’ shiaght keayrtyn. Cha nel aaloayrtys dy kinjagh olk, agh cha nel ny reihderyn laccal clashtyn yn red cheddin reesht as reesht.” Ren mee yn oraid y aaghlenney. Ta'n oraid noa ny s'giare, as ta ny smoo fysseree aynjee: cre ta'n reiltys ceau er scoillyn, er ny raaidyn as er y thie-lheihys.

Jedoonee, 9 Mee Houney. Cha mie lhiam yn noidys eddyr ny partee. Ta fir ennagh jannoo noidys lesh y cheilley ayns ny pabyryn-naight, as cha nel y noidys shen cur bee er boayrd erbee. Dooyrt mee ec y çhaglym mooar: “Cha nel feme ain er noidys. Ta feme ain er sharaghey.” Ta sharaghey er y bushaid feer scanshoil: lhisagh argid y theay goll dys ny reddyn ta sleih feme.

Jemayrt, 11 Mee Houney. Va feysht symoil ec y çhaglym mychione faill. She'n norm ayns ny h-oikyn reiltys, dy vel faill dy chooilley ghooinney goll seose dagh blein, cha nel eh scanshoil cre cho mie as ta e obbyr. Ta mee credjal dy lhisagh toilçhinys ve ny smoo scanshoil na'n norm shen. Ta toilçhinys ec ram sleih aegey, agh t'ad geddyn yn faill s'inshley. Dooyrt reihder elley: “Kys nee oo toilçhinys y howse?” She feysht mie ee, as cha nel fys slane aym foast.

Jerdein, 13 Mee Houney. Laa yn reihys. Hie ny reihderyn dys ny thieyn reihys rish y laa ooilley. Ec mean-oie, haink y naight: va'n staartey aym. Ta mee my oltey jeh Kiare as Feed nish.

Jeheiney, 14 Mee Houney. Ta ram obbyr ry-yannoo. Ta mee screeu rolley: sharaghey 'sy vushaid, faill rere toilçhinys, as thieyn son sleih aegey. Hooar mee screeuyn veih reihderyn jiu, as dooyrt Dewi: “Cooinee er ny reihderyn. Hug ad yn staartey dhyt.”

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n staartey va Morvoren laccal?
V'ee laccal staartey ayns Kiare as Feed.
Cre mychione va ny reihderyn loayrt er y chooid smoo?
Va ad loayrt mychione argid: keeshyn, costys y vee as leagh ny thieyn.
Cre dooyrt Dewi mychione yn oraid?
Dooyrt eh dy row aaloayrtys ayn, as ren Morvoren yn oraid y aaghlenney.
Cre ta Morvoren smooinaghtyn mychione yn norm 'sy reiltys?
T'ee credjal dy lhisagh toilçhinys ve ny smoo scanshoil na'n norm.
Cre haink ec mean-oie er laa yn reihys?
Haink y naight dy row'n staartey ec Morvoren.

lessons.title: Speckleyryn noa son Aoife
lessons.summary: The student Aoife breaks her glasses and leaves the cracked lens with its jagged edge on the counter of Gerens Hosken, a bald optician in Douglas; he measures her eyes to the millimetre, explains why a prism in the lens corrects her sight, compares his price with cheap glasses from the internet, finds comfortable frames that suit the shape of her face, and gives her cleaning fluid for free.
lessons.text:
Ta Aoife ny studeyr ayns Doolish. Cha nel ram argid eck. Un moghrey, hie ee magh as huitt ny speckleyryn eck er y raad. Va'n glonney brisht, as va ymmyl sprangagh er. Cha nel Aoife abyl lhaih gyn speckleyryn, as va screeuyn eck dy screeu roish jerrey yn çhiaghtin.

Hie ee dys shapp Gerens Hosken. She fer-speckleyryn eh, as t'eh er ve gobbraghey ayns Doolish rish feed blein. T'eh meayl: cha nel folt erbee er e chione. Ta'n kione meayl echey soilshey 'sy shapp.

Hug Aoife ny speckleyryn brisht er y boayrd. Ghow Gerens ad, as hug eh e vair er ymmyl sprangagh y ghlonney. “Ta ymmyl sprangagh geyre,” dooyrt eh. Cha nod mee y glonney shoh y chiartaghey. Ta feme ayd er speckleyryn noa.”

Ren eh sooillyn Aoife y howse. Ren eh towse eddyr ny sooillyn eck, millimeadar er millimeadar, son dy vel dagh millimeadar scanshoil ayns speckleyryn. “Ta prismey beg ayns dty speckleyryn,” dooyrt eh. “Cha nel ny sooillyn ayd jeeaghyn er y red cheddin ec y traa cheddin. Ta'n prismey caghlaa raad y toilshey. T'eh karraghey yn aght ta dty hooillyn gobbraghey cooidjagh. Gyn y prismey, bee kione ort.”

Eisht dooyrt Aoife: “Cre'n leagh t'ad? Ta speckleyryn seyr er yn eddyr-voggyl.”

“Ta,” dooyrt Gerens. “Foddee oo speckleyryn y chionnaghey er yn eddyr-voggyl son jeih puint. Agh cha nel ad karraghey dty hilley dy mie, son nagh vel prismey ayndoo, as nagh vel ad jeant rish millimeadar. Ta mee goaill shey feed punt, as ta'n prismey goaill stiagh.”

Va shen ram argid son Aoife, agh ren ee smooinaghtyn er. Cha nel speckleyryn seyr mie dy liooar my nagh vel ad karraghey yn çhilley.

Ren Gerens soilshaghey ram speckleyryn jee. “Ta dagh eddin anchasley,” dooyrt eh. “Ta cummey eddinagh er lheh ec dagh peiagh, as lhisagh ny speckleyryn ve cooie da'n chummey eddinagh shen. Ta eddin cruinn ayd, as bee speckleyryn cheyl jeeaghyn mie ort.” Ren Aoife gearey. “Vel shoh son y çhilley, ny cosmaidagh?” “Daa chooid,” dooyrt Gerens. “Ta'n prismey son y çhilley. Ta cummey ny speckleyryn cosmaidagh: t'eh son yn aght t'ou jeeaghyn. Agh lhisagh ad ve souyr neesht.”

Hug Aoife ny speckleyryn cheyl urree. V'ad souyr er ny cleayshyn as er y stroin. “Ta shoh souyr,” dooyrt ee.

Tra va ny speckleyryn aarloo, ren Gerens boteil beg dy ushlaght y choyrt jee. “Shoh ushlaght son glenney y ghlonney. Cha nel argid erbee er yn ushlaght.” Ren Aoife eeck, as hie ee magh lesh speckleyryn noa. V'ee abyl lhaih reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre haink er speckleyryn Aoife?
Huitt ad er y raad, as va ymmyl sprangagh er y ghlonney.
Cre'n fa ta prismey ayns speckleyryn Aoife?
Er-y-fa nagh vel ny sooillyn eck jeeaghyn er y red cheddin ec y traa cheddin.
Cre'n fa nagh vel speckleyryn seyr er yn eddyr-voggyl mie dy liooar?
Cha nel ad karraghey yn çhilley dy mie, as cha nel ad jeant rish millimeadar.
Vel cummey ny speckleyryn son y çhilley?
Cha nel. Ta'n cummey cosmaidagh, agh ta ny speckleyryn souyr neesht.
Cre hug Gerens da Aoife gyn argid?
Hug eh boteil beg dy ushlaght jee son glenney y ghlonney.

lessons.title: Kiarrooghys
lessons.summary: Diarmuid Cronin, a bus driver in Douglas, loses his wages on horses and at the card tables of a casino while drinking cognac, and a rift opens between him and his wife Muireann, who is eager to save for a house; after an unusual night he is banished from the casino, calls himself a fool, and finds the courage to stop and to give her his bank card.
lessons.text:
Ta Diarmuid Cronin ny ver-bus ayns Doolish. Ta faill vie echey, agh cha nel argid echey ec jerrey yn vee. Ta'n argid echey goll er kiarrooghys. Dy chooilley Jesarn, t'eh goll dys y thie-cloie 'sy valley. T'eh cloie ec y boayrd cloie, as t'eh cur argid er cabbil. T'eh giu coinnagh tra t'eh cloie, as ta'n coinnagh deyr.

Ta Muireann, e ven, gobbraghey ayns thie-lhee. Ta aggindys mooar eck dy chionnaghey thie. T'ee freayll argid ayns y banc dagh mee, as t'ee screeu dy kiart quoid t'ee er hauail. Ta'n aggindys eck dy hauail cha lajer as ta aggindys Diarmuid dy chloie.

Ta skort er çheet eddyr Diarmuid as Muireann. Cha nel ad loayrt mychione argid, son dy vel corree er Muireann. Tra ta Diarmuid çheet thie veih'n thie-cloie, t'ee goll dy lhie. Ta'n skort gaase dy chooilley hiaghtin.

Un Jesarn, va oie neuchadjinagh ec Diarmuid. Ren eh cosney queig cheead punt er cabbil. Eisht ren eh coayl yn argid shen ec y boayrd cloie, as eisht ren eh coayl daa cheead punt elley. V'eh er ve giu ram coinnagh. Ren eh loayrt dy ard as dy olk rish fer y thie-cloie, as ren eh glonney y vrishey er y boayrd. V'eh feer neuchadjinagh da Diarmuid, son dy vel eh dooinney meein er y chooid smoo.

Haink fer-reill y thie-cloie. “Cha nod oo çheet ayns shoh reesht,” dooyrt eh. Va Diarmuid çharbaait veih'n thie-cloie. V'eh çharbaait rish blein slane, as va'n ennym echey er rolley ec y dorrys.

Hie Diarmuid thie dy moal 'sy dorraghys. Va Muireann ny soie 'sy chamyr. Cha row ee er goll dy lhie.

“Va mee my ommidan,” dooyrt Diarmuid. “She ommidan mooar mee. Ta mee er choayl ram argid er kiarrooghys, as ta mee er choayl dty ghraih neesht.”

“Cha nel oo ny ommidan, as cha nel oo er choayl my ghraih,” dooyrt Muireann. “Agh ta'n skort shoh eddyr shin feer vooar. Vel oo dunnal dy liooar dy scuirr?”

Cha row Diarmuid dunnal 'sy thie-cloie, agh v'eh dunnal nish. Hug eh e chaart banc da Muireann. “Freill eh,” dooyrt eh. “Cur argid dou dagh shiaghtin son y bus as son bee. Cha jean mee cloie reesht.” Cha ren eh coinnagh y iu reesht.

Lurg shey meeghyn, va'n skort eddyr oc ny sloo. Va Diarmuid goll dys çhaglym son sleih ta laccal scuirr jeh kiarrooghys. Va argid ayns y banc. Lurg daa vlein, ren ad thie beg y chionnaghey.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n raad ta argid Diarmuid goll?
T'eh goll er kiarrooghys: er y boayrd cloie as er cabbil.
Cre ta Muireann laccal?
Ta aggindys mooar eck dy chionnaghey thie.
Cre'n fa va'n oie neuchadjinagh?
Ren Diarmuid cosney argid as eisht coayl ram, as ren eh loayrt dy olk rish fer y thie-cloie.
Cre haink er Diarmuid lurg shen?
V'eh çharbaait veih'n thie-cloie rish blein.
Cre ren Diarmuid son dy scuirr?
Hug eh e chaart banc da Muireann, as hie eh dys çhaglym.

lessons.title: Yn blog argid
lessons.summary: Eira Nance, a mother in Laxey, writes a blog about living on little money: she does research on prices in the shops, judges each thing she buys by its usefulness, learns sewing to mend her son's clothes until her thumb aches, and writes about the imaginary money that her son Talan uses in a shop game at his infant school.
lessons.text:
Ta Eira Nance cummal ayns Laksaa marish e vac, Talan. Ta Talan queig bleeaney d'eash, as t'eh goll dys y scoill oikanagh 'sy valley. Ta Eira gobbraghey ayns y thie-lioaryn trie laa 'sy chiaghtin. Cha nel ram argid oc, agh ta bea vie oc.

Ta blog ec Eira. She “Argid beg, bea vie” ennym y vlog. T'ee screeu ayns y blog dagh Jedoonee, tra ta Talan ny chadley. Ta sleih ayns Mannin as ayns Sostyn lhaih y blog eck, as t'ad screeu ny smooinaghtyn oc fo dagh art.

Ta ram aahirrey ayns y blog. Dagh shiaghtin, ta Eira goll mygeayrt ny shappyn as t'ee screeu sheese leagh y vee: arran, bainney, oohyn as ooylyn. T'ee jannoo aahirrey er yn eddyr-voggyl neesht. Eisht t'ee screeu 'sy vlog cre'n shapp s'seyr. Ta sleih feer ghennal son yn aahirrey eck, son nagh vel traa oc dy yannoo eh nyn lomarcan.

Ta Eira credjal ayns ymmydoilid. “Roish my ta mee kionnaghey red erbee,” t'ee screeu, “ta mee briaght jeh my hene: cre'n ymmydoilid t'ayn? Jean-ym ymmyd jeh dagh laa, ny un cheayrt 'sy vlein?” Ta ymmydoilid ny smoo scanshoil eck na red aalin.

Ec y toshiaght, cha row Eira abyl whaaley. Tra va towl ayns eaddagh Talan, ren ee kionnaghey eaddagh noa. Eisht ren ee whaaley y ynsagh veih e moir. Ta whaaley feer ymmydoil: ta Eira kiartaghey yn eaddagh oc nish. Un oie, v'ee whaaley ec y boayrd rish three ooryn, as va'n ordaag eck goaill pian. Va'n ordaag goaill pian rish laa slane, agh ren ee gearey mychione 'sy blog: “Cooinee er dty ordaag tra t'ou whaaley!”

Ayns y scoill oikanagh, ta shapp cloie ec ny paitçhyn. Ta argid conrieugh oc: duillagyn pabyr as screeu orroo, as claghyn beggey myr cooinaghyn. Ta Talan creck ooylyn conrieugh as arran conrieugh da ny paitçhyn elley. Haink eh thie un laa as dooyrt eh rish e voir: “Ta mee er chosney jeih punt conrieugh!”

Ren Eira screeu art 'sy vlog mychione y shapp cloie. “Ta paitçhyn ynsagh mychione argid tra t'ad cloie lesh argid conrieugh,” hug ee 'sy vlog. “Ta Talan toiggal nish dy vel dagh red ceau argid.” Va ny smoo sleih lhaih yn art shen na art erbee elley 'sy vlog rish y vlein ooilley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n ennym t'er y vlog ec Eira?
She “Argid beg, bea vie” ennym y vlog.
Cre'n aahirrey ta Eira jannoo dagh shiaghtin?
T'ee goll mygeayrt ny shappyn as t'ee screeu sheese leagh y vee.
Cre ta Eira briaght jee hene roish my t'ee kionnaghey red?
T'ee briaght cre'n ymmydoilid t'ayn.
Cre haink er Eira tra v'ee whaaley?
Va'n ordaag eck goaill pian, son dy row ee er ve whaaley rish three ooryn.
Cre'n argid t'ayns y shapp cloie ec y scoill oikanagh?
Ta argid conrieugh ayn: duillagyn pabyr as claghyn beggey.

lessons.title: Yn taishbynys beg
lessons.summary: A small travelling circus comes to Castletown for a week, but its money is short: Hedra Bastian, an adventurous acrobat, hurts her thigh and cannot perform, the drummer Fionn plays louder to cover the gap, the ringmaster cracks his whip, a magic act and a marmoset fill the evening, and in the end the injury insurance and a full Saturday tent save the week.
lessons.text:
Haink taishbynys beg dys Balley Chashtal son shiaghtin. Ta'n taishbynys goll veih balley dys balley, as ta cloiederyn ayn ta lheim, daunsey as cloie kiaull. Cha nel ram argid ec y taishbynys. Ta'n argid ooilley çheet veih ny tiggadyn, as ta feme oc creck tiggadyn dy liooar dagh oie dy eeck son bee, son y thie-oast as son faill ny cloiederyn.

Ta Hedra Bastian ny skibbyltagh 'sy taishbynys. T'ee aeg as contoyrtagh. Tra v'ee aeg, v'ee dreeym sleityn as lheim veih creggyn 'sy cheayn. Nish t'ee goll seose ayns yn aer er teadyn, as t'ee çhyndaa trooid yn aer. She contoyrtagh firrinagh ee: cha nel aggle urree roish red erbee.

Ta drummeyder 'sy taishbynys neesht: Fionn. T'eh soie ec ymmyl y laare, as t'eh cloie y drummey tra ta'n skibbyltagh goll trooid yn aer. She drummeyder mie eh. Tra ta Hedra lheim, ta'n drummeyder cloie dy bieau as dy ard.

Ta fer-reill y taishbynys ny hassoo 'sy vean. Ta scuitçh echey. Cha nel beishtyn erbee 'sy taishbynys, agh s'mie lesh ny paitçhyn sheean y scuitçh. Tra ta'n scuitçh jannoo sheean ard, ta ny paitçhyn gearey.

Er yn nah oie, va skielley ec Hedra. Huitt ee veih ny teadyn er y laare, as v'ee goaill pian 'sy shleayst. Hie ee dys y thie-lheihys. Dooyrt y fer-lheihys: “Ta'n skielley shoh beg, agh cha nod oo lheim rish shiaght laa. Ta feme ec y shleayst er aash.”

Cha nod y skibbyltagh lheim, as va shen olk son y taishbynys. Va ny smoo na lieh ny tiggadyn creckit son Hedra. Ren fer-reill y taishbynys smooinaghtyn. Ren eh caghlaa yn oie. Hoshiaght, ren fer elley obbyr phishagagh: ren eh ooh y chur ass shilley, as hooar eh yn ooh ayns cleaysh paitçhey. Va'n obbyr phishagagh feer vie, as va ny paitçhyn yindyssagh.

Eisht haink y marmaseen. Ta marmaseen beg ec ben y fer-reill. Ta'n marmaseen soie er e geaylin, as t'eh goaill bee veih e laue. Cha nel y marmaseen jannoo obbyr erbee, agh ta sleih laccal jeeaghyn er y marmaseen. Ren Fionn cloie y drummey dy ard, as va sheean y scuitçh ry-chlashtyn reesht as reesht.

Va argid ec y taishbynys son skielley. Ren yn argid shen eeck son ny laaghyn dy aash ec Hedra. Er y Jesarn, va'n taishbynys lane. Va Hedra ny soie faggys da'n drummeyder, as v'ee jeeaghyn er yn obbyr phishagagh. Lurg yn oie, ren y fer-reill yn argid y choontey. Va dy liooar ayn.

Feyshtyn:
Cre veih ta argid y taishbynys çheet?
T'eh çheet veih ny tiggadyn.
Cre'n fa ta Hedra contoyrtagh?
Cha nel aggle urree roish red erbee, as t'ee goll seose ayns yn aer.
Cre'n skielley va ec Hedra?
Huitt ee veih ny teadyn, as v'ee goaill pian 'sy shleayst.
Cre ren fer-reill y taishbynys son yn oie?
Ren eh obbyr phishagagh as y marmaseen y chur roish ny sleih.
Cre ren eeck son ny laaghyn dy aash ec Hedra?
Ren yn argid son skielley eeck son ny laaghyn shen.

lessons.title: Craueyn y mammoth
lessons.summary: When quarry workers blast rock with dynamite they find mammoth bones and fragments of an old wooden stockade; Macsen Tregaskis, the director of the museum in Douglas, has no money for a new exhibition, so scientists look inside the bones with neutrons, an ambassador from Norway gives money because of the barbed Viking arrowheads found beside the stockade, and the old telegraph room and the story of the old cable crossing to England bring in more visitors.
lessons.text:
Va fir goaill claghyn ass slieau faggys da Doolish. Ren ad ymmyd jeh dynamite dy vrishey y chreg. Lurg y dynamite, va towl mooar 'sy thalloo, as 'sy towl va craueyn mooarey. Va ny craueyn ro vooar son cabbyl ny booa. She craueyn mammoth v'ayn.

She beishteig vooar va'n mammoth, goll rish elefant, lesh folt liauyr. Va'n mammoth cummal ayns Mannin roish thousaneyn dy vleeantyn, tra va'n ellan feer feayr.

Ta Macsen Tregaskis ny stiureyder er y thie-tashtee ayns Doolish. Haink eh dys y slieau, as v'eh feer ghennal. Agh va feysht mooar echey: argid. Cha row argid ec y thie-tashtee son taishbynys noa. Ta taishbynys noa ceau ram argid: son obbyr, son soilshey, as son glenney ny craueyn.

Ren ny fir sheiltyn red elley 'sy thalloo: smooiraneyn fuygh. Va ny smooiraneyn shen ayns linney, goll rish boalley. Dooyrt Macsen: “She sonnagh v'ayn: boalley fuygh mygeayrt shenn valley. Ren sleih y sonnagh shoh dy reayll ad hene noi noidyn.” Faggys da'n sonnagh, hooar ad sideyn yiarn lesh wheddyryn orroo. Ta wheddyr er y side: cha nod oo yn side y hayrn magh ass beishteig, er-y-fa dy vel y wheddyr greimmey er.

Hug Macsen ny craueyn as ny smooiraneyn dys ollooscoill ayns Sostyn. Ren ny oaylleeyn ymmyd jeh naeearaneyn dy yeeaghyn çheu sthie jeh ny craueyn gyn ad y vrishey. Ta naeearane ny ayrn feer veg jeh dy chooilley stoo. Ta naeearaneyn goll trooid craue, as t'ad soilshaghey cre t'ayns y chraue. Ren ad toiggal eash ny reddyn neesht. Va'n mammoth shiaght thousane jeig dy vleeantyn d'eash. Va'n sonnagh as ny sideyn lesh wheddyryn tree cheead jeig dy vleeantyn d'eash: veih'n traa va sleih veih Norlynn reill Mannin.

Cheayll ambasseydeyr Norlynn mychione ny sideyn. Haink yn ambasseydeyr, Solveig Haugen, dys Doolish. “Ta'n shennaghys shoh scanshoil da Norlynn neesht,” dooyrt yn ambasseydeyr. Hug reiltys Norlynn argid da'n thie-tashtee son y taishbynys noa.

Ta shamyr shenn ayns y thie-tashtee neesht: shamyr y çhellegraf. Roish y çhellvane, va sleih cur çhaghteraghtyn lesh çhellegraf. Roish ymmodee bleeantyn, va tead tessenagh soit fo'n cheayn eddyr Mannin as Sostyn, as va'n çhellegraf goll veih'n ellan dys Sostyn. Ren Macsen soilshaghey y çhellegraf shenn as skeeal y tead tessenagh ayns y taishbynys noa.

Va ram sleih çheet dys y taishbynys. Va ny paitçhyn laccal fakin y mammoth, as va ny shenn sleih laccal fakin y çhellegraf. Va argid ny tiggadyn ny smoo na roie.

Feyshtyn:
Cre ren ny fir er y slieau?
Ren ad ymmyd jeh dynamite dy vrishey y chreg.
Cre hooar ad 'sy towl?
Hooar ad craueyn mammoth, smooiraneyn fuygh jeh sonnagh, as sideyn lesh wheddyryn.
Kys ren ny oaylleeyn jeeaghyn çheu sthie jeh ny craueyn?
Ren ad ymmyd jeh naeearaneyn dy yeeaghyn çheu sthie jeh ny craueyn.
Cre'n fa hug Norlynn argid?
Er-y-fa dy row ny sideyn veih'n traa va sleih veih Norlynn reill Mannin, as ta'n shennaghys shen scanshoil da Norlynn.
Cre va'n tead tessenagh?
Va tead tessenagh soit fo'n cheayn eddyr Mannin as Sostyn son y çhellegraf.

lessons.title: Lheim son y thie-chiarail
lessons.summary: To raise money for the hospice that cared for her father, Peigi Scobie does a sponsored parachute jump on a mild day, taught by Cian Doran, an instructor with a strong Irish accent; her brother Ruan walks the coast path past a vertical cliff with other walkers; Peigi lands in a muddy field and comes home soiled, and the money they raise buys a morphine pump for the hospice.
lessons.text:
Va ayr Peigi Scobie ching rish bleeaney, as rish ny meeghyn s'jerree echey, v'eh ayns y thie-chiarail. Va'n sleih va gobbraghey ayns shen feer vie rish. Tra va pian echey, hug ad morfeen da, as va'n morfeen cur aash da. Lurg baase e ayr, dooyrt Peigi: “Ta mee laccal argid y hirrey son y thie-chiarail.”

Cha nel argid dy liooar ec y thie-chiarail. T'eh geddyn argid veih'n reiltys, agh ta lieh yn argid çheet veih'n theay. Ta morfeen deyr, as ta feme ec y thie-chiarail er jeshaght noa dy chur morfeen da ny sleih ching ec y traa cooie.

Ren Peigi reih red dunnal: lheim lesh parashuit. Ren ee screeu da'n lught-thie eck as da ny caarjyn eck: “Cur argid dou son y lheim.” Hug ad ram argid.

Ta Cian Doran ny er-ynsee son lheim lesh parashuit. T'eh veih Nerin, as ta sheeanane lajer echey. Tra t'eh loayrt Gaelg, ta'n sheeanane echey goll rish Yernish. Cha row Peigi toiggal dagh fockle ec y toshiaght, son dy row'n sheeanane cho lajer. Agh ren ee clashtyn rish dy kiart. Dooyrt Cian: “Ny jean aggle y ghoaill. Ta'n parashuit mie. Bee oo tuittym jeeragh sheese hoshiaght, as eisht nee'n parashuit fosley.”

Va'n laa meiygh: va'n emshir feer vie, as cha row geay vooar ayn. “Ta laa meiygh mie son lheim,” dooyrt Cian.

Haink braar Peigi, Ruan, dy akin ee. Cha nel Ruan laccal lheim, agh she shooilleyder mie eh. Ren eh shooyl er raad y traie son argid, marish shooilleyderyn elley veih'n thie-chiarail. Hie ny shooilleyderyn seose er creg phontreilagh, as v'ad jeeaghyn sheese er y cheayn. Va'n chreg phontreilagh ard as aalin.

Lheim Peigi veih'n etlan. Huitt ee jeeragh sheese. Eisht hie'n parashuit fosley, as hie ee sheese dy moal. Va'n magher fliugh, as ren ee tuittym 'sy laagh. Va'n eaddagh eck sollit, as va'n folt eck sollit neesht. Agh v'ee gennal.

Ren Ruan gearey tra honnick eh ee. “T'ou sollit!” dooyrt eh. “Ta,” dooyrt Peigi, “agh ta'n argid ain.”

Hooar ad tree thousane punt. Ren y thie-chiarail jeshaght noa y chionnaghey son y morfeen.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ren Peigi argid y hirrey?
Son y thie-chiarail, va er choyrt kiarail da e ayr.
Cre'n fa nagh row Peigi toiggal dagh fockle ec Cian?
Son dy row'n sheeanane echey cho lajer.
Cre'n emshir va ayn er laa yn lheim?
Va'n laa meiygh, as cha row geay vooar ayn.
Cre ren Ruan son yn argid?
Ren eh shooyl er raad y traie marish shooilleyderyn elley, as hie ad seose er creg phontreilagh.
Cre'n fa va Peigi sollit?
Ren ee tuittym 'sy laagh ayns magher fliugh.

lessons.title: Lessoonyn ayns traa quaranteen
lessons.summary: When the island goes into quarantine, the teacher Gwenllian Matheson and her brother Sorley lose their usual pay and start paid online lessons from their kitchen: she teaches biology, from the pistil of a flower to the zygote, and he teaches religion, from theism to the prophets and the Lenten fast, which also helps the family spend less on food.
lessons.text:
Tra haink doghan noa dys Mannin, va'n ellan ooilley ayns quaranteen. Cha row sleih abyl goll magh dys nyn obbyr, as va ny scoillyn dooint. Va Gwenllian Matheson as e braar Sorley nyn ynseydee ec scoill vooar ayns Doolish. Va'n scoill dooint 'sy quaranteen, as cha row faill slane oc.

“Ta feme ain er argid,” dooyrt Gwenllian. “As ta paitçhyn ayns ny thieyn oc gyn lessoonyn. Lhisagh shin lessoonyn y chur er yn eddyr-voggyl.” Ren ad shen. Va'n chamyr oc ny hie-scoill. Va paarantyn eeck queig puint son dagh lessoon.

Ren Gwenllian bea-oaylleeaght y ynsagh. Er y chied laa, ren ee soilshaghey blaa da ny paitçhyn. “Shoh yn pistil,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n pistil ayns mean y vlaa. Ta'n pistil goaill stoo veih blaa elley, as eisht ta rass gaase.” Ren ny paitçhyn jeeaghyn er y pistil er yn eddyr-voggyl.

Er yn nah hiaghtin, ren ee loayrt mychione sigoat. “Tra ta killag veih'n ayr as killag veih'n voir çheet cooidjagh, ta sigoat ayn,” dooyrt ee. “Ta'n sigoat yn chied killag jeh beishteig noa. Ta'n sigoat scarrey ayns daa chillag, eisht kiare, eisht hoght.” Va'n lessoon mychione y sigoat feer symoil da ny paitçhyn.

Ren Sorley credjue y ynsagh. Ren eh loayrt mychione jeeaghys. “Ta jeeaghys yn credjue dy vel Jee ayn,” dooyrt eh. “Ta jeeaghys ayns ram credjueyn mooarey er y theihll.” Eisht ren eh loayrt mychione phadeyryn. “Phadeyr: shen peiagh ta gra dy vel e fockle çheet veih Jee,” dooyrt eh. “Ta skeealyn mychione phadeyryn 'sy Vible.”

Eisht ren Sorley loayrt mychione y trostey. “Ta trostey ayns ram credjueyn,” dooyrt eh. “Rish daeed laa roish feailley mooar 'syn arragh, cha nel credjuee ennagh gee feill. Ta credjuee elley freayll trostey rish yn laa ooilley, as cha nel ad gee agh ec yn oie. Ta'n trostey jannoo yn credjue oc ny s'lajer, t'ad gra.”

Ren y lught-thie oc trostey neesht 'sy traa shen. Cha row ad gee feill. Ren ad sauail argid er bee, as va shen mie, son nagh row faill slane oc.

Lurg three meeghyn, va'n quaranteen harrish. Hie ny paitçhyn dys y scoill reesht. Agh dooyrt paarantyn ennagh: “Jean-jee ny lessoonyn er yn eddyr-voggyl y reayll.” Nish, ta Gwenllian as Sorley ynsagh er yn eddyr-voggyl dagh Jesarn, as ta faill elley oc.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa nagh row faill slane ec Gwenllian as Sorley?
Va'n scoill dooint 'sy quaranteen.
Cre'n boayl ta'n pistil ayns blaa?
Ta'n pistil ayns mean y vlaa.
Cre ta sigoat?
She yn chied killag jeh beishteig noa eh.
Cre ta jeeaghys, rere Sorley?
She yn credjue dy vel Jee ayn.
Cre'n fa ren y lught-thie sauail argid?
Ren ad trostey, as cha row ad gee feill.
